messages.subject: Correlated error
parts:
I have one simple teoretical question about difference between regression and structural equation. I have red a lot, but still can not cope with "error" :( I will use simple analogy for my model. Now in Croatia is very hot. I can think of the beer model:
Y (dependent) variable is Enjoying beer (let say visaual analog scale (VAS) from 0 to 10 cm or from 0 to 100mm),
And the independent variable are :
X1 = beer price , X2 = beer temperature, and X3 is beer quality. So let say that beer quality (some impact factor from 1 to 100 given by some beer experts) and beer price are higly correlated, let say r = 0. Let say that beer temperature and VAS enjojing beer r = -0.8. (increase of beer temperature decrese VAS). My question, if I use regression, i will get just prediction of Y, and error is everything that is not explained. If I use SEM, would error be different from linear regression error? If I use correlated error from beer quality and beer price, because it is the similar technique that explain quality and determine the price, how woud it affect the model?
Thank You very much.

messages.author: b207b6a270f65efc
messages.subject: Re: Correlated error
parts:
Hi
I hope you receive a complete answer for your question. I hope my answer will be useful but it is not complete. Also I think it is better to discuss such queiosn in https://listserv.ua.edu/archives/semnet.html. 

Simply, in ordinal regression, measurement error in predictors are ignored (or it is assumed that they are free from error). but in SEM you can assume predictors are indicators of a latent variable (this should be logical) and include measurement error in indicatorsm, then use the latent variable (that are free from error)  for prediction of dependent variables. HTH
